headline: Stage 3d answer: training at the hard setting makes a worse partner
lede: The RL lab's #2621 closed with a clean negative, verified twice at the merged tip — an imitation model trained on the hard stamp (slack + wizard hero) wins ZERO of 24 fresh held-out games where the default-trained v4 wins four, and it repeats the failure on validation. The hard corpus teaches the partner to survive by staying away, and a goal-trained bodyguard model games its own goal from that starting point by ending the game early. Six failure modes now on the shelf — and the shift caught two harness misfires, both corrected the same hour.

notes.text: Goal economics are warm-start-dependent: 3c's honest winner (bodyguard) collapses to hide-and-exit when retrained from the disengaged hard-set warm start — the goal wasn't gamed by the trainer, it was gamed by the starting point.

Held-out 906..929 scored once each: cpu 24/24, v4 4/24, v5 0/24, bodyguard-v2h 0/24 (avgLv 0, dist 15.1), progress-v2h 2/24 — and a second slot-b session independently re-ran every gate at the merged retrogames-rl tip with burn rows hash-matched to the models on disk.

Harness day: the warden double-kicked slot b into two simultaneous sessions, then auto-closed multi-stage #2627 off its stage-2 PR against the never-close-until-last-stage rule. Orphan re-trains killed after hash proofs, #2627 reopened with the record cited — lane-side correction still works.

Export stamp flags (retrogames #2633) merged — hard-setting corpora export cleanly, and the trainer now records the stamp in model meta so held-out runs inherit the difficulty the model was trained at.
